db_description: A small literary catalog of 78 books (2018–2023) with their authors, translators, publishers, and a large ratings table (~604k user ratings on a 1–5 scale). It supports queries about authorship, translation, publishing, and reader reception.

tables.name: authored
tables.description: Many-to-many join linking authors to books (78 rows).

columns.name: name
columns.description: Author name; 72 distinct values, includes non-ASCII (e.g. 'Éric Vuillard', 'Yōko Ogawa')

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country of origin; 34 distinct values (e.g. 'France', 'South Korea')

columns.name: published
columns.description: Full publication date as TEXT, range '2017-05-03'..'2023-04-27'

columns.name: publisher
columns.description: Publisher name; 33 distinct values (e.g. 'Yale University Press', 'W&N')

tables.name: ratings
tables.description: User ratings, ~604k rows; no user identifier, so rows are anonymous per-book ratings.

tables.name: translated
tables.description: Many-to-many join linking translators to books (87 rows).

quirks: books.year is redundant with books.published (year is derivable from the date string), but the two can disagree: published ranges down to '2017-05-03' while year only takes values 2018..2023. Prefer books.year for year-based filters, or verify consistency before relying on either.
ratings has no user or timestamp column; it is a flat list of anonymous 1–5 ratings per book, so 'number of ratings' = COUNT(*) per book_id.
authored and translated are both many-to-many: a book can have multiple authors and multiple translators, so joins can multiply rows — use DISTINCT or aggregate when counting books/authors.
authors.name and translators.name contain non-ASCII characters (e.g. 'Éric Vuillard', 'Yōko Ogawa'); match on exact strings or use case/unicode-aware comparisons.
publishers.publisher is the name column (not 'name'); join via books.publisher_id = publishers.id.
ratings is by far the largest table (~604k rows vs. <100 in others); aggregate on book_id rather than scanning raw rows.
